title: Publisher Tile: Voice & Integration Primer (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, shareable primer for partner engineering, product marketing, and listing owners building a publisher tile for cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP). It focuses on: voice & microcopy that converts, technical integration checkpoints, the minimum viable asset set for QA, and a small risk rubric to decide go/no-go.

Context & audience:
- Audience: marketplace product managers, partner engineers, solutions engineers, and partner marketing leads.
- When to use: during a partner onboarding sprint (week 0–2), or when preparing an updated tile for a new region or compliance tier.
- Goal: reduce back-and-forth on copy/legal assets and speed acceptance by cloud marketplaces.

Quick summary of outcomes we want on the tile:
1) Clear value claim in 10 words or less.
2) One sentence of differentiation vs. managed endpoints or native cloud services.
3) Concrete CTA and trial gating instructions (what user will get in trial).
4) Bulleted top 3 benefits tied to measurable metrics (latency/cost/reliability).
5) Minimal technical assets to pass marketplace QA.

Voice & microcopy guidance (short):
- Voice: pragmatic, engineering-friendly, trust-forward. Avoid fluff. Use metrics when possible.
- Tone: concise, confident, permissionless (e.g., "Deploy in minutes — pay per use").
- Avoid hyperbole: replace "best" with "low-latency" or "predictable throughput".
- Do not mention internal roadmap dates or "coming soon" features on the tile.

Short description (for tile, 1 line):
- Option A: "Low-latency LLM inference with predictable throughput and enterprise controls."
- Option B: "Run open LLMs at production scale — cost-aware, SLA-ready inference."

Long description (350–550 chars suggested):
- Draft: "Redwood Inference provides a production-grade LLM inference platform that balances latency, cost, and reliability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Integrate with your cloud account to provision reserved capacity, monitor token-level cost, and route requests by policy. Includes rollout controls, model catalog, and observability for SREs and ML teams."

Feature bullets (3–5 short bullets):
- "Hosted API, dedicated pools, and private VPC deployments"
- "Token-level cost and latency breakdowns in Console"
- "Canary rollouts, automatic fallback, and tracing hooks"
- "Workload-aware batching and KV prefix caching to lower unit costs"

Suggested CTA copy variations (choose one based on channel):
- "Get started — free trial" (PLG/SMB)
- "Request dedicated capacity" (enterprise flow)
- "Contact sales for private deployment" (regulated industries)

Minimum asset checklist (for partner engineering and PM to deliver):
- Marketplace tile copy (short + long + 3 bullets) 
- Two screenshots: Console overview (cost dashboard) and Deployment topology (dedicated capacity) 
- 1 short video (30–60s) optional but recommended: product tour/highlights 
- Lead form/contact email for enterprise flows (verified alias) 
- Logo (SVG, white/bg variants) and 3 descriptive tags/categories 
- Security/compliance stub: short statement + link to SOC2/KMS page (if customer-facing)
- Billing SKU mapping doc and test account with sample usage (for meter validation teams)

Technical integration gate checklist (SRE/partner eng):
- Auth: ensure marketplace IAM role follows provider spec and maps to a test project/tenant.
- Provisioning: CLI/API that creates a demo instance or trial key (script + README).
- Telemetry: sample telemetry events for provisioning success/failure and cost events (document event names).
- Test accounts: one trial account with seeded usage for QA (include credentials or ephemeral test flow).
- Billing: test meter emits to provided SKU with sample 10–100 requests so billing can validate consumption.
- Region parity note: list minimum regions we support for listing (e.g., us-east-1, europe-west1).

Marketplace QA acceptance criteria (conservative, fail-fast):
- Copy matches approved legal language and brand guidelines.
- Screenshots show realistic data (no PII, no placeholder strings like "lorem").
- Trial flow completes end-to-end within 10 minutes for a reviewer.
- Billing event observed in the marketplace test harness during QA.
- Security stub present and links to public compliance docs or a private review doc.

Lightweight risk rubric (help decide go/no-go for MVP tile):
- High risk: billing integration fails, or trial provisioning requires manual steps > 5 mins. -> Block launch.
- Medium risk: screenshots or copy need rework, but technical flow works. -> Ship with "preview" or limited release.
- Low risk: cosmetic copy changes only, telemetry and billing validated. -> Proceed.

Roles & responsibilities (recommended):
- Listing Owner (PM): final copy sign-off, coordinate screenshots, submit listing ticket.
- Partner Eng (PE): provisioning scripts, test accounts, billing meter validation.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): sample scripts, quickstart, screenshot prep.
- Marketing: video, long-description polish, localization requests.

Localization & accessibility notes (minimum for first-pass):
- Localize short and long description to EN/FR/DE for EU launch.
- Ensure screenshots have alt-text descriptors in listing metadata if provider allows.

Examples of quick copy variants to A/B test (save these as snippets):
- Variant 1 (engineering): "Predictable LLM inference — dedicated capacity, transparent costs, and SRE controls."
- Variant 2 (product): "Add LLM features with low latency and predictable pricing."
- Variant 3 (business): "Deploy LLMs for customer-facing features with enterprise SLAs."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we get a dedicated sandbox project from AWS test team for billing validation? (assigned: Diego)
- Confirm SKU mapping for Dedicated vs Hosted trial (assigned: Tom)
- Legal: finalize short security stub language and publish public compliance doc link (assigned: Maya)

Submission timeline (suggested 2-week sprint):
- Day 0–2: final copy + screenshots + screenshots review
- Day 3–6: partner eng implements provisioning and billing smoke tests
- Day 7–9: internal QA + telemetry verification
- Day 10–12: marketplace submission and address reviewer feedback
- Day 13–14: contingency buffer / emergency fixes

Notes to reviewers:
- Keep examples metric-forward (latency in ms, cost delta %, throughput TPS) if you have reliable numbers. If not, use qualitative phrasing instead of placeholder metrics.
- This doc is intentionally lean — use as a checklist during handoffs.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-19: initial skeleton and copy options (Asha)
- 2024-12-05: added technical gate checklist and telemetry notes (Diego)
- 2025-01-21: updated risk rubric and submission timeline (Maya)

-- end of primer --
